answer: Each agent must lock a scarce onyx bond that stays visible in a public mirror established peers can query. In a cooling window they compare the applicant's work trail with that mirrored collateral; reused bonds or conflicting histories are slashed and frozen at once. Passing agents receive one unique marble ledger entry — address, bond height, and first attested epoch — so later graders reject any second plaque that recycles the same lock. A clone cannot cheaply obtain another onyx deposit or a distinct marble record, so sybil swarms collapse under capital and delay rather than a blacklist.
